issue.title: ref_library extra_pass_and_additive_id_resolution wall-clock ratio check flakes under full lib suite load

task_type_fields.evidence:
Proposed by bob-cli-ho.2 note #3 (epic bob-cli-ho, phase period_ids); triaged by bob-cli-ho.land.

- Observed: one failure under the full `cargo test -p bob-obsidian --lib` suite load on athena
  (2026-11-05, while bob-cli-ho.2 ran the full lib suite); the phase reran it in isolation and it
  passed on the same tree. The failure message was not recorded.
- Land agent reran it three times serially on master 44c5c8c8: 3/3 pass (0.05 s each).
- Fail rate: 1 of 1 observed full-suite runs by ho.2; 0 of 4 isolated runs.

Likely root cause (read, not proven): `src/native/ref_library/tests.rs:957` asserts
`extra_time <= additive_time * 20`, two wall-clock durations returned by
`blocked_by::measure_id_resolution`. Under parallel suite load either measurement can be
preempted, so a sub-millisecond `additive_time` lets one scheduler stall in `extra_time` break the
20x ratio. The count assertion (`extra_n <= additive_n`) is deterministic and is not the suspect.
Fix direction: keep the deterministic count check; make the timing check robust (best-of-N
samples, CPU time, or a floor on `additive_time`) or move it behind an explicit perf gate, rather
than widening the ratio. Compare closed sibling flakes bob-cli-ca, bob-cli-gz (load-sensitive
perf gates).

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-ho.2 saw this ref_library test fail once under full-suite load and pass in isolation; its 20x wall-clock ratio assertion is load-sensitive and no tracker exists.

payload.description: Sibling load-sensitive wall-clock perf-gate flake in the lib suite; same fix pattern
